I’m starting with the workspace contract, then I’ll apply the required wake-visual inspection skill before touching the policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t use external research.

The wake-visual skill applies directly here because the request requires a multi-wake policy decision grounded in rollout keyframes. I’m using it to structure the evidence review before any policy edit.

The assigned guidance identifies a narrow local anchor: terminal anterior allocation `0.10` improved three metrics over `0.35`, while full unload `0.0` regressed in three repeat evaluations. I’m now checking the actual sampled observation/metric records and inherited optimizer notes so the next mechanism changes a distinct signal rather than reopening that closed bracket.

The visual comparison is consistent with the metrics: all three `0.10` anchors are byte-identical rollouts, and the posterior-increase failure is nearly the same upper-return trajectory. The fish’s mean x speed exceeds local advection and its positive-y exit occurs against near-zero mean y flow, so the missing capability is bounded terminal course recovery—not propulsion or wake exploitation yet.

Two additional negatives now close the allocation/sideslip branch: posterior allocation `0.55` and `0.75` both worsen navigation around the `0.65` anchor, and even the inherited strict-gated lateral-velocity correction preserves the same `6.609L` minimum and upper exit while worsening mean/final range. I’ll record that diagnosis first, then test one isolated mechanism: modest anterior joint-rate damping only after the existing deep-rearward dual-opening selector activates.

The candidate is now isolated to one new owned parameter and one gated anterior-rate term; the durable guidance has been materially revised to close posterior allocation on both sides and record the strict-gated sideslip negative. I’m checking the exact diff and then invoking the prescribed workspace checker—no CFD rollout.
